clue.text: Lost no time carrying rubbish to be dumped

indicators.note: one word carrying another holds it inside, so the hurry word is wrapped round the rubbish word

parts.note: someone who lost no time sped along
crap is slang for rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone hurried off with a load of rubbish to throw away at the tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost' tempts you towards missing or mislaid, but 'Lost no time' is one idea, hurrying; 'to be' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scrapped has been thrown out or abandoned as useless, the same sense as discarded.

clue.text: Footprints we produce with a smile?

definitions.text: Footprints we produce with a smile?

parts.words: Footprints we produce with a smile?
parts.note: read the footprints as the marks a black bird leaves, and as the creases at the corners of the eyes that smiling makes

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the fine wrinkles beside the eyes, said to look like a bird's footprints, which deepen when we smile.

clue.text: Bet on this letter bringing a whole range of letters

definitions.text: Bet on this letter bringing a whole range of letters

parts.words: Bet on this letter bringing a whole range of letters
parts.note: add the word bet onto the end of this Greek letter and you get the word for the full set of letters

explanation.surface: A gambler stakes money on a single letter and wins a whole range of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The first Greek letter followed by BET spells ALPHABET, the 'whole range of letters'. 'Bet' looks like a wager but is the word to tack on.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first letter of the Greek script, and it heads the word for the complete set of written letters.

clue.text: Making a late entrance, a player gets ordered off

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the place it happens: the late are the dead, who enter heaven through this gateway

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are ordered off in a new sequence, just as a player sent off leaves the field

explanation.surface: A footballer arriving late onto the pitch is promptly sent off by the referee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The late' are the dead, so a late entrance is the way into heaven, St Peter's gateway; 'ordered off' rearranges A PLAYER GETS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christian tradition the gates of heaven are made of pearl, the entrance the departed pass through after death.

clue.text: Rob's lip does tremble

indicators.note: letters that tremble are shaken about, so these words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A robber's lip quivers nervously as he goes about his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tremble' rearranges LIP DOES; the 's after 'Rob' only links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To despoil is to strip a place or person of valuables by force, a synonym of plunder.

clue.text: Awesome female banker

definitions.meaning: a formidable, strong woman, from the warrior women of myth
crossword sense: something with banks, i.e. a river

explanation.surface: A formidable woman works as a banker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' suggests money, but a river 'banks' too, and this river is the longest in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazons were fearsome warrior women of Greek legend; the great South American river has banks, so in crossword terms it is a banker.

clue.text: A non-Protestant cut off from the circle

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic, a Christian who is not Protestant

explanation.surface: A Catholic is excluded from a circle of Protestant friends.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is geometric: a piece cut off a circle's circumference.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry this is a section of a circle's curved edge, a portion separated from the full round.

clue.text: Mary's ill — a belladonna lily brought this about

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words are brought about, turned round into a new order that makes this flower

explanation.surface: Mary has fallen ill, and a poisonous belladonna lily was to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought this about' rearranges MARYS ILL A; here the S of Mary's counts as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The belladonna lily is the common name of a South African bulb whose botanical genus has this name.

clue.text: The main account one broadcast

indicators.note: seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: The chief bank statement is read out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges AC and ONE. 'The main' is an old poetic phrase for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry calls the open sea the main, as in the Spanish Main, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Circle by circle in dance

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other, so the round letter goes inside the dance word

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
the letter O is round like a circle

explanation.surface: Dancers move round in a circle, one ring after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside HOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoop is a ring of wood or metal, round in shape like a ring.

clue.text: Hangs out with mates

definitions.meaning: spends time in the company of

explanation.surface: Someone spends their free time with their friends.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense (keeps company with) and the noun sense (partners) are two readings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To associate with people is to keep company with them, and associates are companions or partners.

clue.text: Be unwell after animal's attack

indicators.note: the sick word comes after the animal word, so it is placed second in the answer

parts.note: an ass is a donkey, an animal
to ail is to be ill

explanation.surface: A sick beast lashes out at its keeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animal's' supplies its word with the possessive dropped, so the 's gives no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail someone is to launch an assault on them, physically or with words.

clue.text: Remote trip, taking in extremes of Lombardy

indicators.note: one word taking in another holds it inside, so the trip word surrounds the pair of letters

parts.note: an outing is a day trip

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A trip to a far-flung spot in northern Italy calls at both ends of Lombardy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes of' takes Lombardy's first and last letters only, and 'taking in' wraps the trip word round them.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlying area lies far from the centre, so it is distant or remote.

clue.text: Don't take this too seriously, it's only a flipping game

definitions.text: Don't take this too seriously, it's only a flipping game

parts.words: Don't take this too seriously, it's only a flipping game
parts.note: flipping sounds like a mild curse, but the game is literally played by flipping small discs into a cup

explanation.definitionFit: This children's game is played by pressing on the edge of counters so they flick up into a pot, a trivial pastime.

clue.text: Live, when hauled out of lake, muddy and dripping

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

indicators.note: here out of means outside, so the hauled word sits outside the letter for lake

parts.note: dragged means pulled or hauled
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Someone pulled from a lake emerges alive but soaked and filthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' is read as 'outside', so the hauling word goes round the lake letter, making DRAGGLED; 'when' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedraggled describes a person or animal made wet, dirty and untidy, as if trailed through mud.

clue.text: Illustrate, with regard to the here and now

annotationWithheld.clue: Illustrate, with regard to the here and now

clue.text: It's bound to get cut away to a point

parts.note: to lop is to cut away branches
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: A rope is meant to be trimmed back so that it tapers to a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' is a leap, not tied up; LOP plus E. 'It's', 'to get' and 'to a' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lope is a long, easy bounding stride, as of a running wolf.

clue.text: A hole in the roof of the mouth makes one quiver

indicators.note: one piece is put in the other, so the hole word goes inside the mouth word

parts.note: the palate is the roof of the mouth
a pit is a hole in the ground

explanation.surface: A hole in the roof of someone's mouth makes them tremble.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'A' before 'hole' is only an article, and 'makes one' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To palpitate is to throb or tremble, especially of a fast-beating heart.

clue.text: Block the way to work

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: Something obstructs the route to the office.
explanation.walkthrough: ST plus OP; 'the' and 'to' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop something is to halt or obstruct it, just as a barrier blocks a road.

clue.text: Reconstructing trellis? Yes, with no flagging

indicators.note: something reconstructed is built again in a new form, so these letters are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A gardener rebuilds a trellis, agreeing to keep at it without a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reconstructing' rearranges TRELLIS and YES. 'Flagging' suggests flags or paving, but means tiring.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something tirelessly is to keep going without weariness, the opposite of tiring.

clue.text: By miracle, characters recover

indicators.note: the characters, or letters, of the word are redistributed to form a new word

explanation.surface: By some miracle, the people in the story get well again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' tells you to rearrange the letters of MIRACLE; 'By' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim something is to get it back or recover possession of it.

clue.text: Conifers, source of this type of medicine?

annotationWithheld.clue: Conifers, source of this type of medicine?

clue.text: Wild animal briefly appeared — nothing made a sound

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
rang means a bell made a sound

explanation.surface: A wild beast suddenly appeared, but nothing stirred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' marks the shortened form of orang-utan; 'appeared' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Orang is the short form of orang-utan, the red-haired great ape of Borneo and Sumatra.

clue.text: Old sky creature seen in victory

indicators.note: the animal is seen in the victory word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a win is a victory
an elk is a large deer, a creature

explanation.surface: In ancient times a creature appeared in the heavens as a sign of victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' marks the definition as archaic: this is a poetic word for the heavens, as in the carol line about the welkin ringing.
explanation.definitionFit: Welkin is an old poetic word for the heavens or the vault of the firmament.

clue.text: First lady squeezed in the French reception

indicators.note: the first woman is squeezed in the French article, placed inside it

parts.note: le is a French word for the
Eve, in the Bible the first woman

explanation.surface: The First Lady is crammed into a crowded reception for the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' is the Bible's first woman, not a president's wife; 'squeezed in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A levee was a monarch's morning reception, and later a formal gathering for guests.

clue.text: This form of transport arrived at school carrying student

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'This form of transport arrived at school carrying student' parses CAME + L + TRAIN = CAMEL TRAIN, but the answer as held is CAMSLTRAIN, and the fix is refused because crossing 15-down (held as corrupted REPPRESET) has S in that cell
annotationWithheld.clue: This form of transport arrived at school carrying student

clue.text: Leaves, getting in hot water

parts.note: leaves going into a pot of boiled water to brew, not someone departing who lands in trouble

explanation.definitionFit: The drink is made by steeping dried leaves of an Asian shrub in boiling water.

clue.text: Small girl and boy sharing one bottle

indicators.note: the name shares its space with the number, taking the letter for one inside it

parts.note: Val is a short name used both for girls (Valerie) and boys (Valentine)
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A little girl and a boy share a single bottle of pop.
explanation.walkthrough: VAL is short for both a girl's and a boy's name; 'sharing' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A vial is a small glass container for liquids such as medicine.

clue.text: Ruler taking hat off to her

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish commander or ruler

indicators.note: the hat word is off, knocked out of shape so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A monarch doffs a hat in respect to a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges the hat word into THA; 'taking' and 'to' only link, so 'her' alone is the definition, standing for a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha is a girl's name, so it can stand for a woman referred to by a pronoun.

clue.text: Muscle demanded of uncle backing restive steer

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the uncle's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the United States

indicators.note: a restive animal will not keep still, so the letters of the word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A restless bullock asked something of its uncle's back muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns SAM into MAS; 'restive' rearranges STEER into SETER. 'demanded of' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The masseter is the jaw muscle that closes the mouth for chewing.
